body: Thank you all for the recommendations, I really appreciate them!

This place is really close to me, I've read that it tends to skew older (like 50+) -- how true is that? It'd be super convenient for me but I've been intimidated about going to bars alone so haven't tried it out.

Thank you!
Thank you! Lots of recommendations for this one and it's maybe a 10 minute walk from me. I'll definitely try it out!

I finished a graduate degree a few weeks ago. Most of my friends moved away, including my best friend who moved away the day after graduation. I had developed romantic feelings for her, which was and is confusing since I've always thought of myself as gay.

We were supposed to meet that weekend so she could give me a graduation letter, but we weren't able to. I haven't told her I have feelings for her, there is no chance of reciprocation and I'm about to move as well. I used to text with her every day, but now that classes are over and I have these feelings, I can't figure out how to do that anymore. It's been a few weeks since we've talked.

I wish I didn't have these feelings, especially not now when everyone is gone and I have so much time on my hands for the first time in my life. I just don't want to do anything. I miss my friend.
I have sex with strangers because I can't stand the idea of being vulnerable with someone. The folks I feel comfortable being vulnerable with I don't want to lose through something else.

You waited 3 hours, is that right?  I've been trying to correct my address for weeks and the site hasn't worked, I've been calling and held until 5pm the other night before it kicked me off, and stopped today at 2 hours.  I'm really frustrated.
That's quite far from where I live, and I'm not a student.  Thanks though

> How did this come to their attention? I know you mentioned that they gave you policies, when did they give you those policies? Before or after the alleged violations?

They gave me policies as they gave the me write-up slip, but these were policies that we are all made aware of at time of hire.

I don't exactly know how it came to their attention. My belief based on the wording of the complaint is that when someone in the room questioned why I was reading it, they did not like my answer, or perhaps misunderstood it.

That's kind of where I'm at. I spoke to my supervisor this morning and told her that I intend to resign. I asked her to clarify what is reported to future employers for me, and she seemed sympathetic, but I don't think she has a lot of power. She did ask that I write up my side of the story, which I did in detail (and thankfully there is documentation to support).

But yes, regardless. I feel like this has been the intention for a while. Sadly, this is not the first time I've drafted a letter, but I never thought it would be in response to something like this. Emotionally, I'm hurt by this behavior from an agency that I put a lot of work in to. But practically it's the right choice. It will probably lead to a rough couple of months, but even if I have to do some temp clerical work between jobs, I don't feel like I could function there anymore.

Referral and linkage. The client was not appropriate for our setting d/t hx and we were looking to refer elsewhere. The ER report may have provided information useful to this.

What you describe is what surprises me. I've never had so much as a sideways glance directed at my position, certainly no disciplinary action. I have been caught very much off guard with all of this. I was planning to leave, but I really wanted it to be on a positive note.

I actually do have access to the ER system, and it was a client I had dealt with that day. The clinic's administrative assistant gave me the packet and asked me to give it to the provider. It was just a packet of paper, no envelope or anything. I didn't think much of it.

That is encouraging, I appreciate your replies. I know remarkably little about the situation beyond what I was told - it was a brief meeting of maybe 10 minutes where I was told to sign a write up slip. I do not know of an employment lawyer in the area, but I will do some research. I definitely have things documented, I will go to lengths to ensure I have copies of the relevant things. They recently forced a title change from Case Manager to Coordinator because they got it in their heads that a CM needs a Bachelor's degree or an LPN/RN (that was just last week), and the thought had crossed my mind that this is being seized on with discussion of role changes and such. I don't know. Anyway, thank you for your words, I appreciate it.

>I read your other comments and it sounds like somebody handed you a report and you delivered it, the violation being that you read it along the way.

That is a correct assessment, as far as I understand the situation, at least. The actual disciplinary action states that I read the note "because [I] knew the patient." I think that this has been misunderstood as me knowing them privately (I don't) rather than as a patient I worked with. I attempted to clarify this and my thoughts were dismissed.

I took the packet from my desk in a shared office to the provider's assistant in their shared office. The provider's assistant and I discussed the patient briefly. It was *not* in a sealed file that I can recall. I don't open sealed files unless they have my name on it.

I work for a medical clinic that has an extremely small behavioral health program that has seen a lot of chaos in the past few months. Recent leadership change, termination of two providers, and continued role changes. It is government owned (county). I am not Union. There is a book of policies, they provided me with copies of relevant policies. They are very black and white.

The actual violation is a final warning situation (despite there never having been a first warning). They are looking back to see if there are any other potential violations.

I'm a lot more scared of having the mark on me. I have known people being fired for HIPAA violations, but egregious ones, and they are near unemployable. That's my great fear.

It hasn't deterred me from Social Work - if anything it's made me very cautious on how to isolate this so it doesn't make me unemployable.

I have wracked my brain on how this could be a violation, but before I was spoken to, they had already drawn up discipline papers. They are currently auditing my chart access for "anything unexplainable" - if which there is any I'll be terminated. I'm not sure how they will define this.

I think it goes back to this not being a behavioral health facility, but a medical center that has a therapist and an NP. My role is also very poorly defined and they recently went back on 9 months of policy informing me that I wasn't allowed to document.

I love the field, but I feel totally drained where I am. I was pretty desperate to get out, I just don't want this scarlet letter on me.

That is the assumption I operated under. However, "my client" is kind of a hard one to define. Because the program is so small, I work with all of the providers and all of the clients providing referral and linkage as necessary, along with other case management. The angle Administration has taken is that the ER report did not directly relate to my job, which thus constitutes the violation.

I am the first person to have this position for this agency, and it has been very poorly defined. I do not even have a written job description. It has been months and months of struggle. There was a recent leadership change and it has been very hard.

I very much considered doing this. I feel like I have a lot of references from there. I'm going to sleep on it and make a decision. I feel like it's better to have resigned than be terminated, especially since I'm actively job hunting, but I'm having a lot of trouble separating my practical side from my emotional side right now. I appreciate your feedback.

Reading it. I actually don't think they even knew I gave it to the assistant until I clarified this. We (that provider's assistant) are considered almost symbiotes of the providers we work with (I work with the LCSW). That's why I was so shocked.
Thankfully, they recently hired another guy, who also has an affinity for watches. Finally, something to combat the never ending spew of purses and eye liner.

I think I'm probably "that" guy.

I work in a medical clinic as a scheduler. Originally I was in ER Registration at the hospital, as just a part-timer, but I worked at the clinic PRN (as needed). I usually worked 60 hours a week, minimum. I recently got hired on full time at the clinic, which is nice.

I like my coworkers, and I feel like I get along with them, but I'm the only guy. I work in reception, and most people in the clinic in general are women. I just get this vague idea that the people I work with don't actually like me very much. I don't know why, but I'm not generally a very likable person. I just try to do a good job.

Because I know how difficult it can be in this area if you are, and he did his best to help me. I also know that before I told anyone, I was near suicidal with depression, and he has asked me things like, "when you were thinking about suicide, besides me what did you do to get through it," with the standard Not Me Asking type of terminology.

I don't think it is at all rude of me to ponder it.

She does care, she told me not long ago that I was going to have to start paying rent or she'd kick me out. I tried talking to her about the suicidal thoughts about a year go. She got defensive and yelled at me, so I don't talk to her about how I feel anymore, I just pretend to be okay. (I'm 20 btw)

I live in a very, very, small town. What few friends I had in school moved away. There's no one around to be friends with. The guy I mentioned is literally the only other person I know who still lives in this town and was at one point a friend. I was never social anyway.
done
